finding.concern: The symmetric-cone formula combines “r_c=s∘z−σμe” and “μ=⟨s,z⟩/ν”, with ν the sum of the selected barrier parameters. Under the stated Euclidean Lorentz pairing, e=(1,0) has ⟨e,e⟩=1, whereas the selected Lorentz barrier has parameter 2. At s=e and the barrier multiplier z=−∇F(e)/t=2e/t, μ=1/t but s∘z=2μe. Thus the displayed residual is not the centered residual associated with the selected barrier using a common target parameter across factors. The algorithm repeats this normalization. Clarify whether this is deliberately a differently weighted heuristic residual or reconcile its central-path interpretation. This does not invalidate the separately audited gap certificates. For comparison, Vandenberghe's cone solver report, §§2–3, https://www.seas.ucla.edu/~vandenbe/publications/coneprog.pdf, uses the half-log Lorentz barrier and Lorentz degree 1 with this Jordan identity convention.
